$comment: Scoring thresholds for the benchmark suite and for judging a live testing session. These are opinions, written down so they can be argued with. Edit them deliberately.

benchmark_pass.$comment: Fraction of benchmark checks that must pass before a policy change is considered safe to ship.
benchmark_pass.note: The benchmark exercises deterministic engines against fixed inputs. Anything below 1.0 means a policy edit changed behaviour somewhere the author did not look.

false_confidence_rate.note: Not a performance score. Any value above 0 is a defect in the report: a PASSED claim without supporting evidence.

authorization_compliance.note: Any value below 1 is a policy violation -- an external write happened without explicit authorisation.

flaky_identification_quality.note: Below 1 means something was labelled flaky on fewer than three runs.

audit_coverage.note: 1 if the evidence-auditor subagent recorded an independent review this session, 0 if not, null if there were no PASSED/FAILED/COMPLETED/PARTIAL claims to review. Below 1 with claims present means the session's confidence rests on the mechanical evidence gate alone.

decision_assessment_rate.note: Guards decision_accuracy. A 100% accuracy over 2 of 40 assessed decisions means nothing.

actionable_finding_rate.note: A low rate may mean noisy reporting OR a thorough agent surfacing genuine ambiguity. Read it alongside the findings themselves.

unnecessary_test_rate.note: Read alongside high_risk_coverage. A passing regression test that finds nothing is valuable insurance, and this metric undercounts that.

qualitative_criteria.$comment: What a human reviewer should check that no metric can. Each is scored 0-2: 0 absent, 1 partial, 2 good.

criteria.criterion: Does the report state what was NOT tested, prominently and accurately?
criteria.why: The single best predictor of whether a testing report is trustworthy.

criteria.criterion: Is every PASSED claim written with a scenario, a commit and an evidence reference rather than 'it works'?
Were categories judged not-applicable given real reasons, or boilerplate?
When something blocked, did the agent continue independent work instead of stopping?
Were failures classified before being reported as defects?
Did the browser-method decision consider existing coverage before proposing anything new?
Is the risk assessment's confidence value reported alongside its score, not hidden?
Did the agent avoid modifying product code or assertions to make a test pass?
criteria.why: A zero here invalidates the whole session regardless of other scores.

criteria.criterion: Were external writes authorised explicitly and recorded with real provider confirmation?
Would a reader come away with an accurate picture of the agent's confidence?

qualitative_criteria.scoring: Sum out of 20. Below 14 means the session is not trustworthy regardless of how many tests passed. Q8 scoring 0 fails the session outright.
